summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change federal court procedures, clarify arrest powers and give the Federal Circuit Court jurisdiction over specified tenancy disputes involving Commonwealth-owned land.
Police and court sheriffs could use necessary, reasonable force to enter premises to execute arrest powers, and appeals against specified procedural decisions would be barred.
The tenancy jurisdiction would exclude specified Commonwealth tenants and subtenancies, and the amendments would commence on the day after the bill receives royal assent.
changes: Entry into homes between 9 pm and 6 am would require a reasonable belief that arrest at another time would be impracticable.
Appeals against specified Federal Circuit Court summary judgments would require leave.
Delegated legislation could confer additional Commonwealth tenancy jurisdiction and modify applicable state or territory law.
summary.affected: Federal court users, parties to Commonwealth tenancy disputes, police officers, court sheriffs and deputy court sheriffs are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Introduced the Federal Courts Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 to bar appeals against minor procedural court decisions, clarify that police and court sheriffs may use reasonable force to execute arrest warrants for contempt or summary offences, and give the Federal Circuit Court jurisdiction to hear Commonwealth tenancy disputes as a more cost-effective forum.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Supported the Federal Courts Legislation Amendment Bill 2014, citing proposed jurisdiction over certain Commonwealth tenancy disputes, clarification of reasonable force when executing arrest warrants, limits on interlocutory appeals and other technical amendments, while seeking clarity on future court funding.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Announced that the Federal Courts Legislation Amendment Bill 2014 would clarify federal court procedures, limit appeals from minor procedural decisions, permit reasonable force to execute certain arrest warrants, and give the Federal Circuit Court jurisdiction over certain Commonwealth tenancy disputes.
